R0.9 — the fixes GPT's review 2 requires (R128): predeclared plan

Status: PREDECLARED 2026-10-02 ~19:00 CDT, before any code. Ruling R128 (~/ProjectAmp2/REVISION_REGISTER.md): fix what receipts/R0.9-GPT-REVIEW-2.md requires before R0.9 can be accepted, agenda items E-01..E-05, up to and including bundle r3, which is built and NOT sent. Builder: a Claude subagent on the Mac, over SSH to the PX13. The live record is receipts/R0.9-CLOSURE.md, section "R128 build (review 2 fixes): live record". House rules, as R118: no claim without a measurement; every law gets a planted bug only it catches, or the overlap is declared with its reason; references are written and hashed before their first run and never edited to agree with a run; the four frozen crates (cd-core, cd-wire, cd-node, cd-micro) stay byte-identical; every kernel-leg change is a deviation D10+.

Baseline before any edit (18:47:59 CDT, HEAD bceea0d, clean): tools/guards.sh ALL GUARDS PASS; tools/verify_r08_freeze.sh R0.8 FREEZE VERIFIED.

E-01 — an answer is accepted only as THIS attempt's ACK

Design (fixed by the brief; deviations, if any, recorded with their reason).

  • cd_connect::AttemptNonce: a u64 in a private field. Its only constructor is AttemptNonce::fresh(), which reads

8 bytes from /dev/urandom with std::fs::File (std only, no new crate) and returns None if it cannot. It derives Debug, PartialEq, Eq and nothing else (not Clone, Copy or Default), and nothing implements a conversion into it. value() is what a transport encodes in the HELLO.

  • connect(expectation, candidate, transport) keeps its three arguments and makes the nonce ITSELF, once per call. If

the OS gives none, it fails with the new ConnectError::NoFreshNonce and nothing is retargeted. (Mechanism: the body is a private fn road(…, nonce_source) and connect passes AttemptNonce::fresh; the private seam exists only so a unit test can show the no-nonce path. road is not public, so no caller outside the crate can choose a source.)

  • The trait: TransportPeer::retarget(&mut self, cand, attempt: &AttemptNonce). Contract: it begins ONE attempt; any

HELLO the transport sends for this attempt carries attempt.value(); an implementation must either discard every piece of state from a previous attempt, or refuse.

  • The road, in order: (1) the handle is the expected peer; (2) a fresh nonce, or NoFreshNonce; (3) retarget;

(4) transport authentication; (4a) exact-datagram parse; (4b) correlation, NEW: the frame must be Frame::Ack with echo_nonce == attempt.value() — a Frame::Hello is UnexpectedFrame, an ACK with any other echo is the new AnswerNotForThisAttempt; (5) the expected-NodeId comparison, over decoded bytes, only after correlation; (6) the session. A wrong NodeId in a correctly correlated ACK still REACHES step 5 and fails there.

  • The trace (GPT's nc36 point). A new trait method road_step(&mut self, step: RoadStep), default empty, returns

nothing: the road reports each step as it RUNS (auth, parse, correlate, node). ScriptedPeer records retarget in retarget() and the rest through road_step, so its trace is retarget,auth,parse,correlate,node for a session and stops where the road stopped otherwise. The method returns nothing, so a transport cannot steer the road through it. Consequence, declared: nc42's gate nc42_R_road_trait_has_no_route_method lists the trait's methods literally; its expected list gains road_step. Its plant (m42_trait_route, a method returning the route) still trips it.

  • ScriptedPeer records each nonce it is given (nonces()) and builds its answer at retarget from that attempt's

nonce, discarding the previous attempt's: by ScriptedAnswer mode — Ack (default: the honest ACK), AckWrongEcho, UnsolicitedHello (it carries this attempt's nonce and the right NodeId, so only the frame kind can refuse it), and Fixed(bytes) (e.g. an earlier attempt's correct ACK, replayed). with_trailing is kept.

  • The lab probes that implement TransportPeer (lab/r09close/n1_probe.rs, n5_probe.rs, d6_probe.rs,

d2_probe.rs) answer a correlated ACK built from the nonce they are given. Their output lines and the gates of nc42, nc43, nc44 and nc46 are unchanged.

  • The kernel probe's PID-derived nonce (lab/nc35k/probe.rs:58) is removed: the nonce comes from connect().

Observation, not changed: frozen cd-node/src/main.rs:46 derives its hello nonce from the PID the same way. cd-node is frozen, and the listen responder the kernel leg uses (cd-node/src/lib.rs:74-86) echoes whatever nonce the HELLO carries, so the kernel cases are expected to keep their outcomes. That is measured by running them (E-02), not assumed.

E-02 — KernelWgPeer: one attempt per handle, and no secret-printing query

Choice: a handle serves exactly ONE attempt. The first retarget begins it, whatever its outcome; a second retarget is refused at the top, before any kernel call, as RetargetError::Refused with its own note (retarget: refused: this handle already served an attempt; one attempt per handle (D10)). Why not reset: the per-attempt state is not only fields (target, baseline, started, outcome, answer) but the UDP socket's receive queue and datagrams still in flight from the earlier attempt, which can arrive AFTER any reset; a reset that is correct today is one forgotten field from being wrong tomorrow, while a refusal is one line a gate can watch. The probe already makes one handle per call. E-01's correlation is the second line: even if a stale answer were handed over, it would be refused as AnswerNotForThisAttempt (the plant below measures this).

  • KernelWgPeer::open() no longer takes a nonce; retarget keeps attempt.value() and the HELLO carries it.

  • The private key is no longer read. dump() becomes kernel_peers(), built from wg show <if> latest-handshakes,

wg show <if> endpoints and wg show <if> transfer — each one line per peer keyed by its PUBLIC key; none prints the private key or a preshared key. The doc comment says so, and says what the R0.9 code did. The leg's own in-container kdump helper is NOT changed: it reads wg show wg0 dump inside the container and drops line 1 there, which its comment already states truthfully; changing it would change the evidence lines of the four cases. Recorded in D11.

  • The control, in the battery: nc35k gains a section on a FAKE kernel (a wg and an ip shim on PATH that log

every invocation, and a responder on loopback that is the frozen cd-node's own serve_once), BEFORE the lab is deployed: lab/nc35k/reuse_control.rs opens one handle and calls the real connect() twice. It is not kernel evidence and says so. Two pseudo-cases with verdict lines the mutant harness reads (nc35k_mutants.sh learns Q and P):

  • Q, one attempt per handle (law KQ1): W nc35k_Q_W_first_attempt_on_the_handle_is_a_session; R

nc35k_Q_R_a_second_attempt_was_made; K nc35k_Q_K_no_kernel_call_during_the_second_attempt; C nc35k_Q_C_second_attempt_refused (Retarget(Refused)), nc35k_Q_C_the_refusal_names_the_rule.

  • P, no query that prints a secret (law KP1): W nc35k_P_W_the_handle_consulted_the_kernel; K

nc35k_P_K_no_query_that_prints_a_secret (every wg invocation is show <if> with latest-handshakes, endpoints or transfer, or set <if> peer <k> endpoint <a>).

  • Law KQ2, the HELLO carries this attempt's nonce: measured on the real kernel by E and B (the frozen responder

echoes the HELLO's nonce, so E is a session and B reaches the NodeId step only if it is the attempt's) and on the fake kernel by Q's window.

  • The four kernel cases must keep their outcomes (A TransportNotAuthenticated, B NodeIdMismatch with K1's

handshake advanced, E session, U TransportUnreachable). Before: the leg at bceea0d (run 18:48 CDT today, log nc35k-before.log). After: the leg on the R128 tree. Any change of outcome stops the work (R128 brief).

  • Deviations (in docs/r09-nc35-kernel-leg-DEVIATIONS.md): D10 one attempt per handle, open() without a nonce,

the nonce from connect(), and the fake-kernel section with Q; D11 no secret-printing query, with P, and the leg's kdump left as it is; D12 nc35's pinned SHA-256 moves again (E-01's new cases), the old value kept beside it.

  • Mutants (lab/nc35k/mutants-r128.json, mutants-r128.expected; R108's m0–m8 verbatim, their anchors do not

move): m9 the one-attempt guard removed → Q:K,C; m10 the R0.9 dump query restored → P:K; m11 the HELLO carries a PID-derived nonce instead of the attempt's → E:C B:C Q:W (declared: E, B and Q's window all need a correlated answer). The R108 rows gain Q only where a mutant breaks the handle's first attempt on the fake kernel: m2 (the handshake is never found) and m5 (the NodeId comparison always refuses) → Q:W; every other R108 row is unchanged.

E-03 — nc34 compares complete authority observations

  • auth() returns the whole authority line (got, worker, worker_id, locus, evidence_len), and every

comparison requires it non-empty on both sides (nc35 F2's form). nc34 B records authority w1 before and after its eight facts (new gate nc34_B_authority_identical); F's mint and widen gates compare the whole line; a new nc34_F_evidence_count_unchanged names the evidence count read from those lines.

  • Law N34, its plants: R118's m_bind_mints (every bind adds grant evidence), which nc34 missed, must now turn

nc34 B and F red; and a new r128_bind_mints_on_d_hit (only a fact labelled d_hit, which only nc34 records, adds evidence) → nc34's four gates and nothing else. Declared overlap inside N34: the evidence gate is a projection of the line that mint and widen compare; it exists to name what moved.

  • Wording narrowed: nc34 does not have six separate legitimate movers. It shows the snapshot moving under attach and

finalize and the authority line moving under grant, and reads the six verbs from those measurements (mint and widen from the authority line; bind, restore, transfer, close from snapshot fields). The header and the PASS line say that, and no longer say "every one of the six verbs was measured moving".

E-04 — the amendments

  • (a) The boundary gate matches identifier SEGMENTS, case-insensitively (tools/rendezvous_boundary_gate.py, law

B3). Every identifier-like token in code (string literals included, // comments removed) is split at _, at non-alphanumerics and at lower→upper and acronym boundaries, lower-cased, and each segment compared with each name. Exemptions, reviewed and listed in the gate with a reason each: UNIX_EPOCH (std's clock origin). An exemption is an exact token, never a substring rule. nc38's reference is revised before its first run under R128 (dated note; R118's header pre-declared the flip): the four b_ rows (CarrierId, locus_id, Generation, fencing_epoch) now expect B3; new rows p_seg_screaming_locus_id (LOCUS_ID) → B3, p_seg_label_with_hyphen ("fencing-epoch") → B3, p_exemption_is_exact (unix_epoch_fence) → B3, n_unix_epoch (std's UNIX_EPOCH used) → nothing; and two declared blind spots, re-measured every battery: b_plural_anchors (anchors) and b_abbrev_gen (gen).

  • (b) docs/r09-deferred-threat-backlog.md: "so it cannot be missed" removed; the representations and scopes the

guard does NOT cover listed; torn writes, symlink effects and identity substitution stated to matter even without a location map.

  • (c) Coverage wording: N1 (n1-matrix.tsv notes for R>I, R>C, R>E: their strength is principally the structural

absence of a route input; L>I/L>C/L>E structural only, kept; the N1 catalogue row: accounted dispositions, not twenty independently exercised attack channels); nc36 (equal five-step traces on identical normalized inputs, not a proof about every road); nc46 (isolation evidence plus a real fence baseline, not an integrated attack: the scripted episode's session is never delivered to cd-durable). nc46's window gate is renamed from nc46_B_window_the_episode_reached_the_fenced_node to nc46_B_window_the_scripted_episode_returned_a_session, and the catalogue's D2 row names the new gate (a declared reference change, recorded with this reason; no other cell moves).

  • (d) `tools/verify_battery.py` enforces the REQUIRED inventory itself: the 27 legs in battery order, each with an

exact verdict line (a whole line, anchored at its start: ALL GUARDS PASS; NCnn PASS alone or followed by — …; R0.8 FREEZE VERIFIED: …; run_r08's receipt: receipts-lab/R0.8-<stamp>.json result: PASS), exactly one, and no FAIL verdict for that leg anywhere in its log; the N1 and catalogue checks always on. Laws: V1 leg_inventory_complete, V2 leg_inventory_has_no_extra_or_repeat, V3 leg_<x>_reached_its_subject (exact), V4 the table checks always on. Plants (~/build/r128/vlaw_plants_r128.sh, reference in its header, hashed before it runs, run on the R128 battery's receipt, and each also against the R118 verifier from git for contrast): R118's four rows kept (v0, v_n1_only, v_cat_only, v_unnamed); v_missing_leg (nc33 removed) → V1 only; v_extra_leg (an nc99 with a log saying NC99 PASS) → V2 only; v_repeated_leg (nc33 twice) → V2 only; v_marker_in_prose (nc33's verdict line demoted into a longer line) → V3 only; v_fail_after_pass (NC33 FAIL (1). after the PASS line) → V3 only; v_no_nc41 → V1 and the catalogue check (declared: V4 matters only when nc41 is absent, which V1 also refuses; the catalogue names nc41's gates). Stop conditions (from the brief)

A frozen crate would have to change; the kernel leg cannot run; any of A, B, E, U changes outcome; a law cannot get a plant only it catches. Any of these stops the work and is reported, not improvised around.
